title: The hypertrophy series: modulating session timeframe to control volume/intensity
summary: NH frames session length as intra-session frequency, a form of frequency that most lifters ignore. He argues that intense days should be shorter and volume days longer, that every day should open with strength work rather than splitting intensity and volume across days, and that relevant intensity windows plus progression are what compress training time.
claims: The claim that training longer than an hour and a half is pointless is a myth because it ignores volume and intensity
Session length is a form of frequency: intra-session frequency, meaning how much you do, how long you rest between sets and how sets follow each other
A day with only low reps accumulates a lot of damage in a very high intensity window; a mix of rep ranges is more complete
The rep range mix does not need to repeat in the same pattern every day
Lower-rep exercises are done faster, which saves session time
Programming a session means fitting the most quality work into as little time as possible so you can recover and progress
When programming, ask whether you can get back to baseline to tire the muscle again without risking injury, and whether that work stays in a relevant intensity window
The most strenuous days should be shorter; don't pile volume after a heavy deadlift
A day built on a less taxing, higher-rep squat or floor-pull variation is the place to add more volume
Don't split intensity and volume into separate days; that produces volume without intensity and intensity without volume
Regulate it on a spectrum instead: strength work at the start of every day, with some days more intense and some more volume-heavy
More intense days should be shorter and more voluminous days longer, and a long day should be followed by a less taxing one
Test any program in the gym; if it takes two hours on paper, expect about 30 more minutes, then trim
Long sessions mostly waste time in pointless rest and irrelevant intensity windows; compress them
As you advance you need more tonnage; get it without lengthening sessions by using relevant intensity windows and progression
Progression can be slow, but it must be there; you can't stay at 225 for a decade
Tonnage across sessions should move up and down on a continuum without ever bottoming out or maxing out
